title: N5 Practice Exam, Chapters 1 to 5
intro: Two practice exams that review Chapters 1 to 5. The vocabulary exam has 40 questions, eight from each chapter, and the reading exam has 14 questions on three short passages. Each question is worth 1 point. Give yourself 25 minutes for both, and try to finish in 20.

sections.html:
Exam 1, Chapter 1: Copula sentences

Supply the best word from the choices to complete each short dialogue. The choices are in romaji, like the vocabulary exam in class.

#QuestionYour answer
1A: hajimemashite. jon desu. B: hajimemashite. maria desu. ____ yoroshiku onegaishimasu. (a) douzo (b) sayounara (c) konnichiwa (d) oyasumi
2A: kochira wa donata desu ka. B: tanaka san desu. sakura kaisha ____ shachou desu. (a) wa (b) no (c) ka (d) mo
3A: sumimasen. otearai wa ____ desu ka. B: achira desu. (a) dare (b) dore (c) doko (d) itsu
4A: wan san wa chuugokujin desu. B: aa, sou desu ka. wan san no kotoba wa ____ desu ne. (a) nihongo (b) eigo (c) kankokugo (d) chuugokugo
5A: maria san no gokazoku wa? B: watashi no ____ wa kaishain desu. (The blank means my older brother.) (a) ani (b) oniisan (c) ane (d) otouto
6A: sore wa nan desu ka. B: ____ wa pasokon desu. (B is holding the computer.) (a) are (b) kore (c) sore (d) dore
7A: ano ____ wa donata desu ka. B: kaisha no shachou desu. (a) kore (b) koko (c) kata (d) dochira
8A: wakarimasu ka. B: iie, wakarimasen. ____ onegaishimasu. (a) hajimemashou (b) oyasumi nasai (c) sayounara (d) mou ichido

Exam 2, Passage 1: A self-introduction

Read each passage, then choose the best answer to each question. A few words carry the reading in parentheses, the way the book shows furigana, and the choices are in kana.

わたしの名前(なまえ)は マリアです。フィリピンじんです。いま、日本(にほん)の だいがくの りゅうがくせいです。

ともだちの ジョンさんは アメリカじんです。エンジニアです。

わたしの へやは だいがくの りょうに あります。へやの なかに つくえと いすが あります。つくえの うえに パソコンが あります。つくえの したに かばんが あります。

#QuestionYour answer
1マリアさんは なにじんですか。 (a) フィリピンじん (b) にほんじん (c) アメリカじん (d) ドイツじん
2ジョンさんの しごとは なんですか。 (a) せんせい (b) エンジニア (c) がくせい (d) しゃちょう
3マリアさんの へやは どこに ありますか。 (a) かいしゃ (b) えき (c) だいがくの りょう (d) としょかん
4かばんは どこに ありますか。 (a) つくえの うえ (b) いすの うえ (c) へやの そと (d) つくえの した
5つくえの うえに なにが ありますか。 (a) パソコン (b) かばん (c) いす (d) テレビ

かいしゃは ごぜん 8じはんから ごご 5じまでです。まいしゅう 月曜日(げつようび)の ごご 2じに かいぎが あります。

らいしゅうの 金曜日(きんようび)は やすみです。

sections.title: Answer key
sections.html:
Exam 1, Chapter 1: Copula sentences

#AnswerWhy
1(a) douzoAfter hajimemashite, the set phrase is douzo yoroshiku onegaishimasu. It is what you say when you meet someone for the first time.
2(b) nono links two nouns and shows who or what something belongs to. sakura kaisha no shachou means the president of Sakura company.
3(c) dokodoko asks where. dare is who, dore is which one and itsu is when. otearai (washroom) is a place, so you ask doko.
4(d) chuugokugoAdd go to the country name to get the language: chuugoku becomes chuugokugo. English is the odd one out (eigo).
5(a) aniFor your own family use the plain words: ani, ane, chichi, haha. oniisan is for someone else's older brother, ane is your own older sister and otouto is your own younger brother.
6(b) korekore is for things near the speaker, and B is the one holding it. sore would be the thing near A, are is far from both, and dore is the question word.
7(c) katakata is the polite word for person, and donata is the polite word for who, so they go together. kore, koko and dochira mean this, here and which way.
8(d) mou ichidomou ichido onegaishimasu means again, please. It is what you say in class when you did not catch something.

Exam 1, Chapter 2: Existential sentences

#AnswerWhy
9(a) migimigi (right) is the opposite of hidari (left).
10(b) nishiOsaka is to the west of Tokyo, so the word is nishi. higashi is east, kita is north and minami is south.
11(c) imasutanaka san and maria san are people, and people take imasu. arimasu is for things. imasen would say that nobody is there, which does not fit since two names were given.
12(d) arimasuA key and eyeglasses are things, so the verb is arimasu. People and animals use imasu.
13(a) kafekissaten and kafe mean the same thing: coffee shop. depa-to is a department store, honya is a bookstore and resutoran is a restaurant.
14(b) ryouryou is a dormitory, a place where someone can be. Do not mix it up with ryoushin, which means parents.
15(c) tonariyoko, tonari and soba all mean beside in the book, so B is agreeing with tonari. mukou is across, ushiro is behind and shita is under.
16(d) aidaaida means between, and it is used with two things: ginkou to kafe no aida.

Exam 1, Chapter 3: Counting, prices and phone numbers

#AnswerWhy
17(a) happyaku en800 is happyaku. The hundreds 300, 600 and 800 change their sound: sanbyaku, roppyaku and happyaku.
18(b) yonsatsusatsu is the counter for books and notebooks. mai is for flat, thin things like paper, hon is for long things like pencils and ko is for small objects.
19(c) futariani and watashi make two people, and two people is futari. It is one of the special readings, so learn it as its own word, like hitori for one person.
20(d) hassaiEight years old is hassai. The sound changes, so it is not hachisai.
21(a) nedannedan means price. yachin is rent for a room or house, kippu is a ticket and okane is money in general.
22(b) sanzen en3,000 is sanzen. The special thousands are 1,000 (sen or issen), 3,000 (sanzen) and 8,000 (hassen).
23(c) juuniman enJapanese counts in groups of four digits. 120,000 is 12 ten-thousands: juu ni man.
24(d) zenbuzenbu means all or total. The apple and the orange together come to 300 yen in all.

Exam 1, Chapter 4: Time expressions

#AnswerWhy
25(a) mokuyoubiIf today is Wednesday (suiyoubi), tomorrow is Thursday, mokuyoubi.
26(b) kugatsuSeptember is kugatsu. Nine is ku in the month names, not kyuu. kugetsu would mean nine months.
27(c) hatsukaThe 20th has its own reading, hatsuka. It does not follow the usual nichi pattern.
28(d) yoji4 o'clock is yoji. The hour four becomes yo, so it is not yonji or shiji.
29(a) gorogoro goes with a point in time and means around. gurai is for amounts, like about 20 minutes. han would make it 10:30.
30(b) madekara means from and made means until. gozen 9-ji kara gogo 6-ji made is from 9 a.m. until 6 p.m.
31(c) raigetsuIf this month is October, the next month is raigetsu. sengetsu is last month, kongetsu is this month and maitsuki is every month.
32(d) kinouToday is the 10th (tooka), so the 9th (kokonoka) was yesterday, kinou. ototoi is the day before yesterday.

Exam 1, Chapter 5: Span of time

#AnswerWhy
33(a) basude goes after a vehicle: basu de means by bus. aruite already means on foot, so it never takes de. oufuku and katamichi are about tickets.
34(b) nijikankan marks how long something lasts. nijikan is two hours. niji would be 2 o'clock, nifun is two minutes and nijuppun is twenty minutes.
35(c) maemae means before. 2:55 is five minutes before the 3:00 meeting, so 5-fun mae. sugi means after.
36(d) guraigurai means about and goes with an amount of time, here about 15 minutes. goro goes with a point in time instead.
37(a) oufukukatamichi (one way) is already named in the next sentence, so the first word is oufuku, round trip. It costs more because you travel both ways.
38(b) hantoshihantoshi is half a year. hitotsuki is one month, ichinen is one year and ichijikan is one hour.
39(c) zangyouzangyou is overtime. The company closes at 5 but the work goes on until 8. shukudai is homework, arubaito is a part-time job and kaiwa is conversation.
40(d) hikoukihikouki is an airplane. Manila to Tokyo takes about four hours by plane. A ship would take days, and a bicycle or subway cannot cross the sea.

Exam 2, Passage 1: A self-introduction

#AnswerWhy
1(a) フィリピンじんThe passage says フィリピンじんです, so Maria is Filipino. アメリカじん is John.
2(b) エンジニアJohn is described with エンジニアです, so he is an engineer.
3(c) だいがくの りょうへやは だいがくの りょうに あります. ryou means dormitory, and the room is in the university dormitory.
4(d) つくえの したつくえの したに かばんが あります. shita means under, so the bag is under the desk.
5(a) パソコンつくえの うえに パソコンが あります. ue means on top, so the computer is on the desk.

Exam 2, Passage 2: A shop sign

#AnswerWhy
6(b) 120えんノートは 1さつ 120えんです. The 100 yen is for the ballpen and 250 yen is for five pencils.
7(c) 50えん250 yen buys 5 pencils (5ほん). 250 divided by 5 is 50 yen each.
8(d) 220えんThe notebook is 120 yen and the ballpen is 100 yen. Together that is 220 yen. ぜんぶで means in total.
9(a) ごご 7じごご 7じまで means until 7 p.m. gogo is p.m. and made means until. The 9 is the opening hour.
10(b) にちようびやすみは にちようびです. The kanji in the sign, 日曜日, is read にちようび, which is Sunday.

Exam 2, Passage 3: A work week

#AnswerWhy
11(c) 40ぷん40ぷんぐらい かかります means it takes about 40 minutes. ぐらい means about, and かかります means it takes.
12(d) ごぜん 8じはんごぜん 8じはんから means from 8:30 a.m. han means half past, so 8じはん is 8:30.
13(a) まいしゅう げつようびの ごご 2じまいしゅう げつようびの ごご 2じ means every Monday at 2 p.m. maishuu is every week, not next week (らいしゅう).
14(b) きんようびらいしゅうの きんようびは やすみです. Next week's Friday is a day off. Monday is the meeting day, not the day off.

English translations of the passages

Passage 1. My name is Maria. I am Filipino. Right now I am an international student at a university in Japan. My friend John is American. He is an engineer. My room is in the university dormitory. In the room there is a desk and a chair. On top of the desk there is a computer. Under the desk there is a bag.

Passage 2. Minami Bookstore. Notebooks are 120 yen each. Ballpens are 100 yen each. Pencils are 250 yen for five. Open from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Closed on Sundays.

Passage 3. I am an employee of a company in Manila. It takes about 40 minutes from my house to the company by subway. The company runs from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Every week there is a meeting on Monday at 2 p.m. Next week's Friday is a day off.
